11-01.title: Stephen Crane
11-01.description: American author whose vivid Civil War novel The Red Badge of Courage redefined realist fiction despite the fact he had never seen battle himself.

11-01.title: Tim Cook
11-01.description: Apple CEO who took the helm after Steve Jobs and guided the company to become the world's first trillion-dollar corporation.

11-01.title: Aishwarya Rai Bachchan
11-01.description: Bollywood superstar and Miss World 1994 winner, celebrated as one of the most beautiful and globally recognised Indian actresses of all time.

11-01.title: First Thermonuclear Bomb Tested
11-01.description: The United States detonated Ivy Mike on Enewetak Atoll, the world's first hydrogen bomb, vaporising the entire island in a fireball miles wide.

11-01.title: Maastricht Treaty Takes Effect
11-01.description: The treaty establishing the European Union formally entered into force, creating the framework for a common currency and European citizenship.

11-01.title: MTV Unplugged in New York — Nirvana
11-01.description: Nirvana's posthumous acoustic masterpiece, recorded months before Kurt Cobain's death, became one of the most haunting and best-selling live albums in rock history.

11-01.title: Harriet
11-01.description: Cynthia Erivo's Oscar-nominated portrayal of Harriet Tubman traces the abolitionist's daring escape from slavery and her legendary Underground Railroad missions.

11-02.title: Marie Antoinette
11-02.description: Austrian archduchess who became Queen of France and a symbol of royal excess before meeting her fate at the guillotine during the French Revolution.

11-02.title: Burt Lancaster
11-02.description: Acrobat-turned-actor whose athletic grace and intensity anchored classics from From Here to Eternity to Elmer Gantry, earning him an Academy Award.

11-02.title: David Schwimmer
11-02.description: American actor who made the neurotic paleontologist Ross Geller on Friends one of the most beloved television characters of the 1990s.

11-02.title: First ISS Crew Arrives
11-02.description: American astronaut Bill Shepherd and Russian cosmonauts Yuri Gidzenko and Sergei Krikalev became the first permanent residents of the International Space Station.

11-02.title: Morris Worm Unleashed
11-02.description: Cornell student Robert Morris released the first widely distributed internet worm, infecting thousands of computers and exposing the fragility of the early internet.

11-02.title: Bohemian Rhapsody — Queen
11-02.description: Freddie Mercury's six-minute operatic rock epic, featuring layered vocal harmonies and a genre-defying structure, became the quintessential rock anthem of its era.

11-02.title: Bohemian Rhapsody
11-02.description: Rami Malek's electrifying Oscar-winning portrayal of Freddie Mercury chronicles Queen's rise and the legendary Live Aid performance that cemented their legacy.

11-03.title: Charles Bronson
11-03.description: Rugged Hollywood action star who became an international icon through The Magnificent Seven and the Death Wish franchise.

11-03.title: Roseanne Barr
11-03.description: Stand-up comedian whose working-class sitcom Roseanne broke television ground in the late 1980s as one of the highest-rated shows of its era.

11-03.title: Gennady Golovkin
11-03.description: Kazakh professional boxer nicknamed GGG, celebrated for his devastating knockout power and a long unbeaten streak as unified middleweight world champion.

11-03.title: Laika Launched into Space
11-03.description: Soviet spacecraft Sputnik 2 carried Laika, a stray Moscow dog, into orbit — making her the first living creature to travel in space.

11-03.title: Panama Declares Independence
11-03.description: A revolutionary junta proclaimed Panama's independence from Colombia, with the United States swiftly recognising the new nation to secure the canal treaty.

11-03.title: "Superstition" — Stevie Wonder
11-03.description: Stevie Wonder's funky clavinet-driven smash hit topped the Billboard Hot 100 and became one of the defining funk songs of the 1970s.

11-03.title: Borat
11-03.description: Sacha Baron Cohen's provocative mockumentary follows a fictional Kazakh journalist across America, holding up a satirical mirror to cultural prejudice with outrageous results.

11-04.title: Walter Cronkite
11-04.description: CBS News anchorman dubbed 'the most trusted man in America,' whose on-air grief at Kennedy's assassination brought the nation together in mourning.

11-04.title: Matthew McConaughey
11-04.description: Oscar-winning Texas actor who reinvented himself with a string of dramatic roles including Dallas Buyers Club after years of romantic comedies.

11-04.title: Will Rogers
11-04.description: Cherokee-American cowboy philosopher and humorist whose witty newspaper columns and radio broadcasts made him one of the most beloved Americans of the 1920s–30s.

11-04.title: NSA Established
11-04.description: President Truman signed a secret directive creating the National Security Agency, the U.S. signals intelligence organisation that would later become the most powerful surveillance body on Earth.

11-04.title: Iran Hostage Crisis Begins
11-04.description: Iranian students stormed the U.S. Embassy in Tehran, seizing 66 American diplomats and triggering a 444-day hostage crisis that defined the Carter presidency.

11-04.title: "I Will Always Love You" — Whitney Houston
11-04.description: Whitney Houston's earth-shattering rendition of Dolly Parton's ballad from The Bodyguard became the best-selling single ever by a female artist.

11-04.title: The Terminator
11-04.description: James Cameron's low-budget sci-fi thriller launched Arnold Schwarzenegger into superstardom and introduced the relentless time-travelling assassin T-800 to pop culture.

11-05.title: Vivien Leigh
11-05.description: British actress whose portrayal of Scarlett O'Hara in Gone with the Wind won her the first of two Academy Awards and cemented her as a Hollywood legend.

11-05.title: Art Garfunkel
11-05.description: American singer whose crystalline tenor formed one of the most celebrated vocal partnerships in pop history alongside Paul Simon.

11-05.title: Bryan Adams
11-05.description: Canadian rock singer-songwriter who scaled the charts with enduring anthems like Summer of '69 and spent a record-breaking 16 weeks at UK #1 with Everything I Do.

11-05.title: Gunpowder Plot Foiled
11-05.description: Guy Fawkes and Catholic conspirators were arrested in the cellars of Parliament just hours before they planned to blow up King James I, giving birth to Bonfire Night.

11-05.title: Susan B. Anthony Votes Illegally
11-05.description: Women's suffrage activist Susan B. Anthony cast her ballot in Rochester, New York despite laws barring women from voting, and was subsequently arrested and fined.

11-05.title: "Bridge Over Troubled Water" — Simon and Garfunkel
11-05.description: The swan song of Simon and Garfunkel's partnership, Art Garfunkel's soaring vocal on this gospel-tinged ballad swept the Grammy Awards and defined an era.

11-05.title: V for Vendetta
11-05.description: Set on November 5th, this dystopian thriller based on Alan Moore's graphic novel gave the Guy Fawkes mask new life as a global symbol of resistance.

11-06.title: John Philip Sousa
11-06.description: The March King whose military marches like 'The Stars and Stripes Forever' became the soundtrack of American patriotism.

11-06.title: Emma Stone
11-06.description: Oscar-winning actress who charmed audiences in Easy A before bringing grace and wit to La La Land, earning her the Academy Award for Best Actress.

11-06.title: Ethan Hawke
11-06.description: American actor and novelist whose decades-long collaboration with director Richard Linklater produced the landmark Before trilogy and Boyhood.

11-06.title: Lincoln Elected President
11-06.description: Abraham Lincoln's election as the 16th U.S. president on a platform opposing the spread of slavery triggered the secession of Southern states and the Civil War.

11-06.title: Meet the Press Debuts
11-06.description: NBC launched Meet the Press, which would become the longest-running television programme in American history, holding politicians accountable for over seven decades.

11-06.title: "I'd Do Anything for Love (But I Won't Do That)" — Meat Loaf
11-06.description: Meat Loaf's operatic rock epic hit #1 on the Billboard Hot 100, becoming the best-selling single in the UK for all of 1993.

11-06.title: Spotlight
11-06.description: This Best Picture Oscar winner meticulously chronicles the Boston Globe investigation that uncovered the Catholic Church's systematic cover-up of widespread child abuse.

11-07.title: Marie Curie
11-07.description: Polish-French physicist who became the first person to win two Nobel Prizes, discovering polonium and radium and pioneering research into radioactivity.

11-07.title: Albert Camus
11-07.description: French-Algerian philosopher and author whose novel The Stranger introduced absurdism to the world and earned him the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1957.

11-07.title: Lorde
11-07.description: New Zealand singer-songwriter who at 16 topped global charts with Royals, a minimalist pop critique of materialism that announced a major new voice.

11-07.title: Bolshevik Revolution
11-07.description: Lenin's Bolshevik Party stormed the Winter Palace in Petrograd, overthrowing the Provisional Government and inaugurating the Soviet state that would reshape the 20th century.

11-07.title: First Woman Elected to U.S. Congress
11-07.description: Jeannette Rankin of Montana was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives, becoming the first woman to serve in the United States Congress, four years before women nationwide could vote.

11-07.title: Titanic: Music from the Motion Picture — James Horner
11-07.description: James Horner's sweeping soundtrack to James Cameron's blockbuster, featuring Celine Dion's 'My Heart Will Go On,' sold over 10 million copies worldwide.

11-07.title: The Theory of Everything
11-07.description: Eddie Redmayne's Oscar-winning performance as Stephen Hawking portrays the physicist's intellectual triumphs and the painful deterioration wrought by motor neurone disease.

11-08.title: Edmond Halley
11-08.description: English astronomer who calculated the orbit of the comet bearing his name, correctly predicting its return and demonstrating the power of Newtonian mechanics.

11-08.title: Kazuo Ishiguro
11-08.description: Japanese-British novelist who won the Nobel Prize in Literature for quietly devastating works like The Remains of the Day and Never Let Me Go.

11-08.title: Gordon Ramsay
11-08.description: Scottish celebrity chef who parlayed Michelin-starred kitchens into a global television empire built on volcanic temper and impossibly high culinary standards.

11-08.title: X-Rays Discovered
11-08.description: German physicist Wilhelm Röntgen accidentally discovered a new form of radiation while experimenting with cathode ray tubes, taking the first X-ray photograph of his wife's hand.

11-08.title: Louvre Museum Opens
11-08.description: The former royal palace of the French kings opened its doors to the public during the Revolution, beginning its transformation into the world's most visited art museum.

11-08.title: Led Zeppelin IV — Led Zeppelin
11-08.description: Led Zeppelin's untitled fourth album, featuring 'Stairway to Heaven' and 'Black Dog,' became one of the best-selling albums in history with over 37 million copies sold.

11-08.title: Skyfall
11-08.description: Sam Mendes' brooding Bond film became the highest-grossing 007 entry ever, with Adele's title song winning the Academy Award for Best Original Song.

11-09.title: Carl Sagan
11-09.description: American astronomer and science communicator whose Cosmos television series and Pale Blue Dot narrative inspired generations to look at Earth through a cosmic lens.

11-09.title: Hedy Lamarr
11-09.description: Austrian-American film star who, alongside composer George Antheil, invented a frequency-hopping spread spectrum technique that formed the basis for modern Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.

11-09.title: Dorothy Dandridge
11-09.description: American actress and singer who became the first Black woman nominated for the Academy Award for Best Actress, for her starring role in Carmen Jones.

11-09.title: Berlin Wall Falls
11-09.description: East Germany opened its borders and jubilant crowds began tearing down the Berlin Wall, the most iconic moment of the Cold War's end and German reunification.

11-09.title: Kristallnacht
11-09.description: Nazi-orchestrated pogroms across Germany and Austria shattered thousands of Jewish synagogues, homes, and businesses in a night of coordinated terror that foreshadowed the Holocaust.

11-09.title: Piano Man — Billy Joel
11-09.description: Billy Joel's debut charting single, drawn from his experiences as a bar room pianist, became his signature song and one of the most universally beloved sing-alongs in pop history.

11-09.title: My Fair Lady
11-09.description: Audrey Hepburn and Rex Harrison star in this lavish Lerner and Loewe adaptation that swept eight Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Best Director.

11-10.title: Martin Luther
11-10.description: German theologian whose Ninety-five Theses nailed to a Wittenberg church door ignited the Protestant Reformation and permanently fractured Western Christianity.

11-10.title: Hugh Grant
11-10.description: British actor whose bumbling-charm persona defined the 1990s romantic comedy through Four Weddings and a Funeral and Notting Hill.

11-10.title: John P. Pemberton
11-10.description: American pharmacist who invented the original Coca-Cola formula in his Atlanta backyard in 1886, inadvertently creating the world's most recognised beverage brand.

11-10.title: U.S. Marine Corps Founded
11-10.description: The Continental Congress authorised two battalions of marines at Tun Tavern in Philadelphia, establishing the United States Marine Corps on the eve of revolution.

11-10.title: Sesame Street Premieres
11-10.description: PBS debuted Sesame Street, the revolutionary children's series that used puppetry, animation, and humour to teach literacy and numeracy to preschoolers across America.

11-10.title: Reputation — Taylor Swift
11-10.description: Taylor Swift's dark, synth-pop reinvention debuted at #1 in 30 countries and became the fastest-selling album by any artist in 2017.

11-10.title: Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri
11-10.description: Martin McDonagh's darkly comic drama, starring Frances McDormand as a grieving mother challenging local police, swept the awards season with incendiary performances.

11-11.title: Fyodor Dostoyevsky
11-11.description: Russian novelist whose explorations of suffering, morality, and the human psyche in Crime and Punishment and The Brothers Karamazov established him as a titan of world literature.

11-11.title: Kurt Vonnegut
11-11.description: American satirist whose anti-war novel Slaughterhouse-Five, inspired by his survival of the Dresden firebombing, became a defining text of 20th-century American literature.

11-11.title: Leonardo DiCaprio
11-11.description: American actor and environmental activist who endured decades of Oscar nominations before winning Best Actor for The Revenant, cementing one of Hollywood's most celebrated careers.

11-11.title: World War I Armistice
11-11.description: At the eleventh hour of the eleventh day of the eleventh month, the guns fell silent on the Western Front as Germany signed the armistice ending four years of devastating war.

11-11.title: Tomb of the Unknown Soldier Dedicated
11-11.description: President Harding dedicated the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery, creating an enduring memorial to unidentified American war dead.

11-11.title: "Imagine" — John Lennon
11-11.description: John Lennon's gentle yet radical hymn to peace and brotherhood became one of the best-selling singles in history and a perennial anthem at moments of global tragedy.

11-11.title: The Fabelmans
11-11.description: Steven Spielberg's luminous autobiographical film traces his childhood discovery of cinema and the complicated family secrets that shaped one of Hollywood's greatest directors.

11-12.title: Grace Kelly
11-12.description: Philadelphia actress who starred in Rear Window and To Catch a Thief before becoming Princess of Monaco in a fairy-tale marriage that transfixed the world.

11-12.title: Neil Young
11-12.description: Canadian rock legend dubbed the Godfather of Grunge, whose restless creativity and fierce independence produced masterpieces from Harvest to Rust Never Sleeps.

11-12.title: Anne Hathaway
11-12.description: American actress who won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for her devastating portrayal of Fantine in Les Misérables.

11-12.title: World Wide Web Proposal Published
11-12.description: Tim Berners-Lee published his formal proposal for the World Wide Web to his supervisor at CERN, laying the blueprint for the system that would transform human civilisation.

11-12.title: Bhola Cyclone Strikes East Pakistan
11-12.description: The deadliest tropical cyclone in recorded history made landfall on the Bay of Bengal coast, killing an estimated 300,000 to 500,000 people in what is now Bangladesh.

11-12.title: Never Mind the Bollocks, Here's the Sex Pistols — Sex Pistols
11-12.description: The Sex Pistols' only studio album detonated punk rock into the mainstream, hitting #1 in the UK and becoming the most controversial record of its generation.

11-12.title: Finding Neverland
11-12.description: Johnny Depp portrays J.M. Barrie in this tender drama about the friendship with a widow's four boys that inspired him to write Peter Pan.

11-13.title: Whoopi Goldberg
11-13.description: American actress, comedian, and talk show host who won the Oscar, Emmy, Tony, and Grammy to become one of the very few EGOT recipients in entertainment history.

11-13.title: James Clerk Maxwell
11-13.description: Scottish physicist whose unified theory of electromagnetism is considered the second great unification in physics after Newton, directly enabling radio, television, and wireless communication.

11-13.title: Gerard Butler
11-13.description: Scottish actor who became an action star with 300, his portrayal of King Leonidas inspiring countless memes and a new era of historical epic films.

11-13.title: Paris Terror Attacks
11-13.description: Coordinated ISIS-linked terrorist attacks struck six locations across Paris, killing 130 people in the deadliest attack on French soil since World War II.

11-13.title: Denny Party Lands at Alki Point
11-13.description: The Denny Party of settlers arrived at Alki Point in present-day Washington State, founding what would become the city of Seattle.

11-13.title: Laundry Service — Shakira
11-13.description: Shakira's crossover English-language debut introduced her trademark belly-dancing pop to global audiences, becoming her best-selling album with over 13 million copies sold.

11-13.title: Mank
11-13.description: David Fincher's black-and-white Netflix film revisits Hollywood's golden age through the eyes of Herman J. Mankiewicz as he writes Citizen Kane.

11-14.title: King Charles III
11-14.description: The longest-serving heir apparent in British history, Charles waited 73 years before ascending to the throne in 2022 following the death of his mother Queen Elizabeth II.

11-14.title: Astrid Lindgren
11-14.description: Swedish author whose irrepressible redheaded heroine Pippi Longstocking became one of the most beloved children's book characters in history, translated into over 70 languages.

11-14.title: Claude Monet
11-14.description: French Impressionist master whose series paintings of haystacks, Rouen Cathedral, and water lilies revolutionised Western art's relationship with light and perception.

11-14.title: Moby-Dick Published
11-14.description: Herman Melville's monumental novel about the obsessive quest of Captain Ahab for the white whale was published in America, initially to mixed reviews before becoming the definitive American novel.

11-14.title: Ruby Bridges Integrates School
11-14.description: Six-year-old Ruby Bridges walked through a crowd of angry protestors under U.S. Marshal escort to become the first Black child to attend William Frantz Elementary School in New Orleans.

11-14.title: "All Along the Watchtower" — Jimi Hendrix
11-14.description: Jimi Hendrix's electrifying reimagining of Bob Dylan's protest song became so definitive that Dylan himself preferred the cover to his own original recording.

11-14.title: Nellie Bly: Around the World in 72 Days
11-14.description: A dramatisation of pioneering journalist Nellie Bly's 1889 race around the globe, which began on this date, as she bet she could beat Jules Verne's fictional 80-day record.

11-15.title: Georgia O'Keeffe
11-15.description: American modernist painter celebrated as the Mother of American Modernism, whose monumental close-up flower paintings and New Mexico desert landscapes stand as icons of 20th-century art.

11-15.title: Erwin Rommel
11-15.description: German field marshal known as the Desert Fox whose brilliant tank tactics during the North Africa campaign earned him respect from both Allied and Axis commanders.

11-15.title: Ed Asner
11-15.description: American actor who won an unprecedented seven Emmy Awards, best remembered as the gruff but warm-hearted Lou Grant on The Mary Tyler Moore Show.

11-15.title: League of Nations First Assembly
11-15.description: The first assembly of the League of Nations convened in Geneva with representatives from 41 member states, representing humanity's first organised attempt at collective global governance.

11-15.title: Brazil Declares Republic
11-15.description: A military coup overthrew Emperor Pedro II, transforming Brazil from a constitutional monarchy into a republic in a nearly bloodless revolution.

11-15.title: "Iris" — Goo Goo Dolls
11-15.description: Written for the City of Angels soundtrack, the Goo Goo Dolls' earnest ballad spent 18 weeks at #1 on Billboard and earned Diamond certification two decades later.

11-15.title: Immortals
11-15.description: Director Tarsem Singh's visually sumptuous retelling of the Theseus myth pits Henry Cavill's warrior king against Mickey Rourke's scheming King Hyperion in a Greek mythological epic.

11-16.title: Diana Krall
11-16.description: Canadian jazz pianist and vocalist who has sold over 15 million albums worldwide and won multiple Grammy Awards, becoming the best-selling jazz artist of her generation.

11-16.title: Lisa Bonet
11-16.description: American actress who captivated audiences as free-spirited Denise Huxtable on The Cosby Show before carving out a distinctive independent film career.

11-16.title: Sanna Marin
11-16.description: Finnish Social Democratic politician who became the world's youngest sitting head of government at 34, navigating Finland through the pandemic and into NATO membership.

11-16.title: Sherman's March to the Sea Begins
11-16.description: Union General William T. Sherman led 62,000 troops out of Atlanta, beginning his devastating 300-mile march to Savannah that shattered Confederate supply lines and civilian morale.

11-16.title: Benazir Bhutto Elected Prime Minister
11-16.description: Benazir Bhutto was elected prime minister of Pakistan, becoming the first woman to lead a modern Muslim-majority nation.

11-16.title: 2001 — Dr. Dre
11-16.description: Dr. Dre's long-awaited comeback album redefined West Coast hip-hop production, went six times platinum, and launched Eminem to global superstardom.

11-16.title: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone
11-16.description: Chris Columbus' faithful adaptation of J.K. Rowling's debut novel introduced Daniel Radcliffe as the Boy Who Lived and launched one of cinema's most beloved franchises.

11-17.title: Martin Scorsese
11-17.description: New York filmmaker whose visceral crime epics — from Taxi Driver to Goodfellas to The Irishman — redefined American cinema and the language of screen violence.

11-17.title: Rock Hudson
11-17.description: Hollywood leading man and romantic icon whose 1985 death from AIDS became the moment that forced mainstream America to confront the epidemic.

11-17.title: Rachel McAdams
11-17.description: Canadian actress who balanced blockbuster appeal in Mean Girls and The Notebook with critically acclaimed dramatic turns in Spotlight and Doctor Strange.

11-17.title: Suez Canal Opens
11-17.description: The 193-kilometre waterway connecting the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea opened, slashing the shipping route between Europe and Asia by thousands of miles.

11-17.title: Nixon's 'I Am Not a Crook' Statement
11-17.description: President Richard Nixon told an Associated Press editors' conference 'I am not a crook' in a moment that instantly became one of the most memorable lines in political history.

11-17.title: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn — First Edition
11-17.description: Mark Twain's groundbreaking novel was published, its vernacular narrative voice and moral confrontation with American racism helping establish it as the foundational American novel.

11-17.title: Casino Royale
11-17.description: Daniel Craig's debut as a rougher, more emotionally vulnerable James Bond rebooted the franchise with visceral action and a genuinely moving love story.

11-18.title: Alan Shepard
11-18.description: The first American in space, who later commanded Apollo 14 and became the only Mercury astronaut to walk on the Moon, famously hitting a golf ball on the lunar surface.

11-18.title: Kirk Hammett
11-18.description: Lead guitarist of Metallica whose scorching solos on Master of Puppets and One are among the most influential in heavy metal history.

11-18.title: Owen Wilson
11-18.description: Texas-born actor whose improvisational charm and distinctive broken nose made him a beloved figure in comedies from Wedding Crashers to Midnight in Paris.

11-18.title: Steamboat Willie Premieres
11-18.description: Walt Disney's Steamboat Willie — the first animated cartoon with synchronised sound — debuted in New York, introducing Mickey Mouse to the world.

11-18.title: Battle of Vertières
11-18.description: Haitian forces under Jean-Jacques Dessalines defeated Napoleon's army at the decisive battle that effectively ended French rule and paved the way for Haiti's independence.

11-18.title: "I Will Always Love You" — Whitney Houston chart run begins
11-18.description: Whitney Houston's power ballad from The Bodyguard began its landmark 14-week reign atop the Billboard Hot 100, making it one of the best-selling singles ever recorded.

11-18.title: Ben-Hur
11-18.description: William Wyler's epic starring Charlton Heston premiered and went on to win a then-record eleven Academy Awards including Best Picture, a feat untouched for nearly four decades.

11-19.title: Jodie Foster
11-19.description: American actress and director who won two Academy Awards before turning 30 — for The Accused and The Silence of the Lambs — cementing her status as one of cinema's finest.

11-19.title: Meg Ryan
11-19.description: America's sweetheart of the romantic comedy era, whose electric chemistry with Tom Hanks in Sleepless in Seattle and You've Got Mail defined a genre.

11-19.title: Tommy Dorsey
11-19.description: The Sentimental Gentleman of Swing whose silky trombone and impeccable big band drove the careers of Frank Sinatra and countless other Golden Age stars.

11-19.title: Gettysburg Address Delivered
11-19.description: President Abraham Lincoln delivered his 272-word masterpiece at the dedication of the Soldiers' National Cemetery, reframing the Civil War as a struggle for human equality.

11-19.title: Anwar Sadat Visits Israel
11-19.description: Egyptian President Anwar Sadat became the first Arab leader to visit Israel, offering a peace plan to the Knesset in a historic act of diplomacy that led to the Camp David Accords.

11-19.title: "9 to 5" — Dolly Parton
11-19.description: Dolly Parton's finger-tapping office-worker anthem hit #1 in both pop and country charts, becoming one of the most recognisable feminist pop songs in American music.

11-19.title: Malcolm X
11-19.description: Spike Lee's sweeping biopic features Denzel Washington's towering performance as the Black nationalist leader, tracing his journey from criminal to transformative civil rights icon.

11-20.title: Robert F. Kennedy
11-20.description: U.S. Attorney General, Senator, and presidential candidate whose assassination in 1968 — coming just months after his brother's — shattered a generation's faith in American politics.

11-20.title: Joe Biden
11-20.description: American politician who overcame personal tragedy to serve as Vice President under Barack Obama before becoming the 46th President of the United States.

11-20.title: Duane Allman
11-20.description: Slide guitar virtuoso and co-founder of the Allman Brothers Band whose fluid mastery of the Dobro shaped Southern rock and influenced every guitarist who followed.

11-20.title: Queen Elizabeth II Marries Prince Philip
11-20.description: Princess Elizabeth married Lieutenant Philip Mountbatten at Westminster Abbey in a ceremony that gave war-weary Britain a rare moment of pageantry and celebration.

11-20.title: Alcatraz Occupation Begins
11-20.description: A coalition of 89 Native American activists occupied Alcatraz Island in San Francisco Bay, beginning a 19-month protest that galvanised the American Indian Movement.

11-20.title: "Theme from Shaft" — Isaac Hayes
11-20.description: Isaac Hayes' wah-wah guitar-driven theme hit #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and won the Academy Award for Best Original Song, the first by a Black composer.

11-20.title: The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou
11-20.description: Wes Anderson's eccentric meditation on obsession, grief, and fatherhood follows Bill Murray's oceanographer on a quest to film the mythical jaguar shark.

11-21.title: Voltaire
11-21.description: French Enlightenment writer and philosopher whose savage wit, defence of civil liberties, and attacks on religious dogma in works like Candide shaped modern secular thought.

11-21.title: René Magritte
11-21.description: Belgian Surrealist painter whose thought-provoking images — bowler-hatted men with apples for faces, pipes labelled 'This is not a pipe' — challenged the nature of representation itself.

11-21.title: Ken Griffey Jr.
11-21.description: Considered by many the greatest all-round baseball player of his era, The Kid's smooth swing and spectacular outfield play graced the Seattle Mariners for a generation.

11-21.title: Mayflower Compact Signed
11-21.description: Forty-one male Mayflower passengers signed the Mayflower Compact, America's first governing document, establishing a model of self-governance that influenced the U.S. Constitution.

11-21.title: First Manned Hot-Air Balloon Flight
11-21.description: Jean-François Pilâtre de Rozier and the Marquis d'Arlandes made the first free human flight in a Montgolfier balloon over Paris, covering nine kilometres in 25 minutes.

11-21.title: "Call Me Maybe" — Carly Rae Jepsen
11-21.description: Carly Rae Jepsen's buoyant pop confection became one of the best-selling singles in history after Justin Bieber tweeted about it, spending nine weeks atop the Billboard Hot 100.

11-21.title: Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge Opens
11-21.description: The Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge linking Brooklyn and Staten Island opened as the world's longest suspension bridge span, a feat of mid-century engineering celebrated in many New York films.

11-22.title: Charles de Gaulle
11-22.description: French general who led the Free French Forces from London during Nazi occupation and later founded the Fifth Republic, serving as its first president.

11-22.title: Scarlett Johansson
11-22.description: American actress who parlayed early indie acclaim in Lost in Translation and Girl with a Pearl Earring into becoming Hollywood's highest-grossing actress as Marvel's Black Widow.

11-22.title: Benjamin Britten
11-22.description: English composer and pianist whose operas Peter Grimes and Billy Budd and his War Requiem established him as the leading British composer of the 20th century.

11-22.title: JFK Assassinated
11-22.description: President John F. Kennedy was shot in his motorcade in Dealey Plaza in Dallas, Texas, a traumatic event that shattered America's optimism and generated decades of conspiracy debate.

11-22.title: Angela Merkel Becomes German Chancellor
11-22.description: Angela Merkel was sworn in as Germany's first female Chancellor, beginning a 16-year tenure that would make her the most powerful woman in European political history.

11-22.title: The Beatles (White Album) — The Beatles
11-22.description: The Beatles' sprawling double album — 30 tracks spanning avant-garde noise, folk, and proto-heavy metal — is one of the most ambitious and influential records ever made.

11-22.title: Toy Story
11-22.description: Pixar's revolutionary debut feature — the first entirely computer-animated film — used talking toys to tell a story about friendship and change that remains a masterpiece of modern cinema.

11-23.title: Boris Karloff
11-23.description: English actor who gave Frankenstein's monster pathos and tragedy in Universal's 1931 horror classic, creating an iconic performance that transcended the genre.

11-23.title: Miley Cyrus
11-23.description: American singer and actress who grew up on screen as Hannah Montana before reinventing herself multiple times, most recently claiming a Grammy with Flowers.

11-23.title: Billy the Kid
11-23.description: American outlaw of the Lincoln County War era whose brief, violent life made him one of the most mythologised figures of the American West.

11-23.title: Pong Released by Atari
11-23.description: Atari released Pong, one of the first commercially successful arcade video games, marking the beginning of the commercial video game industry.

11-23.title: Thespis Performs First Known Acting
11-23.description: Thespis of Icaria became the first recorded actor to portray a character on stage at the festival of Dionysus in Athens, giving all actors the name 'thespians'.

11-23.title: Chinese Democracy — Guns N' Roses
11-23.description: After 14 years in the making, Axl Rose's long-awaited Guns N' Roses album arrived and debuted at #3 on the Billboard 200, becoming a symbol of perfectionist ambition.

11-23.title: Terms of Endearment
11-23.description: James L. Brooks' comedy-drama about a complicated mother-daughter relationship won five Academy Awards including Best Picture and introduced Shirley MacLaine's Aurora Greenway.

11-24.title: Scott Joplin
11-24.description: African-American composer dubbed the King of Ragtime, whose Maple Leaf Rag became the first sheet music to sell over one million copies.

11-24.title: Zachary Taylor
11-24.description: Mexican-American War hero and 12th President of the United States who died of a stomach illness just 16 months into his term, before the slavery crisis reached its breaking point.

11-24.title: Pete Best
11-24.description: The original drummer of the Beatles who was replaced by Ringo Starr just weeks before the band signed with Parlophone and launched to global superstardom.

11-24.title: On the Origin of Species Published
11-24.description: Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species, laying out the theory of evolution by natural selection, sold out on its first day and permanently transformed biology and humanity's understanding of itself.

11-24.title: Lee Harvey Oswald Killed by Jack Ruby
11-24.description: Dallas nightclub owner Jack Ruby shot JFK's alleged assassin Lee Harvey Oswald live on national television, ending any prospect of a public trial and deepening conspiracy theories.

11-24.title: "Maple Leaf Rag" — Scott Joplin
11-24.description: Scott Joplin's jaunty syncopated piano piece became the first sheet music to sell a million copies and ignited the ragtime craze that swept American popular culture.

11-24.title: Planes, Trains and Automobiles
11-24.description: John Hughes' Thanksgiving road comedy pairs Steve Martin's uptight ad executive with John Candy's relentlessly cheerful shower ring salesman in a journey of unexpected friendship.

11-25.title: Andrew Carnegie
11-25.description: Scottish-American steel magnate who built the world's largest corporation then gave away nearly his entire fortune, funding over 2,500 public libraries worldwide.

11-25.title: Joe DiMaggio
11-25.description: The Yankee Clipper, whose 56-game hitting streak in 1941 remains one of the most unassailable records in professional sport, epitomising American elegance.

11-25.title: Percy Sledge
11-25.description: American soul singer whose aching 1966 ballad When a Man Loves a Woman became one of the great recordings of the soul era and a timeless statement of devotion.

11-25.title: The Mousetrap Opens in London
11-25.description: Agatha Christie's murder-mystery play opened at the Ambassadors Theatre in London's West End and would go on to become the longest continuously running stage production in history.

11-25.title: JFK State Funeral
11-25.description: President Kennedy was buried at Arlington National Cemetery after a solemn horse-drawn procession from the Capitol, watched by 95 million Americans on live television.

11-25.title: "When a Man Loves a Woman" — Percy Sledge
11-25.description: Percy Sledge's raw, pleading soul ballad reached #1 in America and became Atlantic Records' first gold single, a template for heartfelt southern soul.

11-25.title: The Godfather Part II
11-25.description: Francis Ford Coppola's Oscar-winning sequel interweaves Michael Corleone's moral descent with flashbacks to young Vito's rise, widely regarded as one of the greatest films ever made.

11-26.title: Tina Turner
11-26.description: The Queen of Rock 'n' Roll who survived an abusive marriage to Ike Turner and then reinvented herself at 44 with Private Dancer, one of the greatest comebacks in music history.

11-26.title: Charles Schulz
11-26.description: American cartoonist whose Peanuts strip, featuring Charlie Brown, Snoopy, and the Peanuts gang, ran for 50 years and became the most widely syndicated comic strip in history.

11-26.title: Willis Carrier
11-26.description: American engineer who invented the modern air conditioner in 1902, transforming where humans could comfortably live and work and enabling the sunbelt population boom.

11-26.title: NHL Founded
11-26.description: The National Hockey League was formed in Montreal with five founding teams, including the Montreal Canadiens and Toronto Arenas, becoming North America's premier professional ice hockey league.

11-26.title: Casablanca Premieres
11-26.description: Michael Curtiz's wartime romance starring Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman premiered at Hollywood's Thanksgiving, eventually winning three Oscars including Best Picture.

11-26.title: "Private Dancer" — Tina Turner
11-26.description: Tina Turner's explosive comeback album yielded four Top 10 singles and won four Grammy Awards, one of the most triumphant second acts in pop music history.

11-26.title: Milk
11-26.description: Gus Van Sant's biopic stars Sean Penn — in his second Oscar-winning performance — as Harvey Milk, the first openly gay elected official in California history.

11-27.title: Jimi Hendrix
11-27.description: Seattle-born guitarist whose pyrotechnic performances, feedback-drenched solos, and psychedelic studio experiments transformed the electric guitar into an instrument of boundless possibility.

11-27.title: Louisa May Alcott
11-27.description: American novelist and abolitionist whose autobiographical Little Women introduced the March sisters to generations of readers and remains one of the most beloved novels in American literature.

11-27.title: Berry Gordy
11-27.description: Founder of Motown Records who turned a $800 loan into the most successful Black-owned business in America, launching the careers of Stevie Wonder, Diana Ross, and Marvin Gaye.

11-27.title: Nobel Prizes Established
11-27.description: Alfred Nobel signed his will establishing the Nobel Prizes in Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature, and Peace — prizes that would honour humanity's greatest achievements for generations.

11-27.title: First Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade
11-27.description: Macy's department store employees marched through Manhattan with floats, live animals from the Central Park Zoo, and bands in what became America's beloved annual Thanksgiving tradition.

11-27.title: "All Too Well (Ten Minute Version)" — Taylor Swift
11-27.description: Taylor Swift's extended re-recording of her most acclaimed song topped the Billboard Hot 100 at over ten minutes, making it the longest song ever to reach #1.

11-27.title: Frozen
11-27.description: Disney's smash animated musical featuring Idina Menzel's world-conquering Let It Go became the highest-grossing animated film of all time upon its release.

11-28.title: Friedrich Engels
11-28.description: German philosopher who co-authored The Communist Manifesto with Karl Marx and financially supported Marx's research, shaping the most influential political ideology of the 20th century.

11-28.title: Jon Stewart
11-28.description: American comedian whose Daily Show on Comedy Central became the most trusted source of political satire for a generation and launched the careers of Stephen Colbert and John Oliver.

11-28.title: Randy Newman
11-28.description: Los Angeles songwriter and composer whose deceptively cheerful melodies often mask biting social satire, and whose Pixar work for Toy Story earned him an Academy Award.

11-28.title: Magellan Enters the Pacific
11-28.description: Ferdinand Magellan's fleet of three battered ships passed through the strait bearing his name at the tip of South America and entered the vast Pacific Ocean, beginning the first circumnavigation of the globe.

11-28.title: Grand Ole Opry First Broadcast
11-28.description: WSM Radio in Nashville aired the first broadcast of what would become the Grand Ole Opry, the longest-running radio programme in U.S. history and the home of American country music.

11-28.title: Bolero — Maurice Ravel (Premiere)
11-28.description: Maurice Ravel's hypnotic orchestral work premiered at the Paris Opera, building a single melody over a relentlessly repeated snare drum rhythm to a thunderous climax.

11-28.title: The Breakfast Club
11-28.description: John Hughes' quintessential 1980s coming-of-age film trapped five high school archetypes in Saturday detention, where their barriers dissolve into one of cinema's most honest portraits of adolescence.

11-29.title: C.S. Lewis
11-29.description: Irish author and Oxford don whose Chronicles of Narnia introduced millions of children to allegory and whose Mere Christianity became a cornerstone of popular Christian apologetics.

11-29.title: Chadwick Boseman
11-29.description: American actor whose portrayal of Black Panther's T'Challa made him a global icon; he filmed his final performances while privately battling stage IV colon cancer.

11-29.title: Mariano Rivera
11-29.description: Panamanian-American closer for the New York Yankees whose devastating cut fastball earned him a career ERA of 2.21 and made him the unanimous first-ballot Hall of Famer.

11-29.title: UN Partitions Palestine
11-29.description: The UN General Assembly passed Resolution 181 calling for the partition of British Mandatory Palestine into separate Arab and Jewish states, triggering the Arab-Israeli War.

11-29.title: Warren Commission Established
11-29.description: President Lyndon Johnson signed an executive order creating the Warren Commission to investigate the assassination of John F. Kennedy, appointing Supreme Court Chief Justice Earl Warren as its head.

11-29.title: "Rolling in the Deep" — Adele
11-29.description: Adele's thunderous gospel-tinged breakup anthem launched one of the best-selling albums of the 21st century and spent seven weeks atop the Billboard Hot 100.

11-29.title: Black Panther
11-29.description: Ryan Coogler's landmark Marvel film starring Chadwick Boseman as King T'Challa of Wakanda shattered box office records and became a cultural phenomenon celebrating African heritage.

11-30.title: Winston Churchill
11-30.description: British Prime Minister and Nobel-Prize-winning author who rallied the Allied world against Nazi Germany with his defiant oratory and unflinching resolve during World War II.

11-30.title: Mark Twain
11-30.description: American author whose Adventures of Huckleberry Finn and The Adventures of Tom Sawyer captured the humour, violence, and moral contradictions of 19th-century America.

11-30.title: Shirley Chisholm
11-30.description: The first Black woman elected to the United States Congress and the first to seek a major-party presidential nomination, famously declaring herself 'unbought and unbossed'.

11-30.title: Thriller Released
11-30.description: Michael Jackson's Thriller was released and went on to become the best-selling album in history, winning a record eight Grammy Awards and transforming music video into an art form.

11-30.title: Winter War Begins
11-30.description: The Soviet Union invaded Finland despite a peace treaty, launching a brutal three-month war in which the outnumbered Finns' fierce resistance shocked the world and embarrassed Stalin.

11-30.title: Thriller — Michael Jackson
11-30.description: Michael Jackson's record-shattering album — featuring Billie Jean, Beat It, and the title track — remains the best-selling album in history with over 70 million copies sold worldwide.

11-30.title: Misery
11-30.description: Rob Reiner's adaptation of Stephen King's novel features Kathy Bates in her Oscar-winning role as Annie Wilkes, the devoted fan who becomes the most terrifying captor in horror history.
